# Walk In Tubs Houston

> WalkInTubsHouston.com helps homeowners, seniors and caregivers in the Houston area (Houston, Harris County and nearby suburbs from Katy to Conroe, Galveston to Baytown) choose and install walk-in tubs, wheelchair-accessible transfer tubs, roll-in showers and walk-in showers. Part of the Aging Safely Baths family; installs are done by Aging Safely Baths. BBB Accredited with an A+ rating. Quotes by phone at 1-888-779-2284 (BATH) or through the online quote form. Prices are quoted per home and are not published on the site.

## Main pages

- [Walk-in tubs Houston (home)](https://walkintubshouston.com/): Tub types, safety features, white-glove installation, Houston house factors (slab foundations, second floors, water heaters, electrical), funding overview, local resources, service-area ZIP codes, roll-in shower overview with an interactive 3D model, FAQ.
- [Walk-in tub buying guide](https://walkintubshouston.com/walk-in-tub-buying-guide/): Fit for the bather, measuring, sizes and seat height, door styles, fill and drain time, hot water, hydrotherapy, materials, scald protection, installation, cost factors, warranty questions, checklist.
- [Contact and quote request](https://walkintubshouston.com/contact/)
- [Privacy policy](https://walkintubshouston.com/privacy-policy/)

## Houston guides

- [Walk-in tub cost in Houston](https://walkintubshouston.com/walk-in-tub-cost-houston/): National ranges from Fixr (most projects about $3,500 to $10,000) and This Old House (about $1,800 to more than $20,000), the Houston house details that move a quote, and how to read a quote line by line.
- [Paying for a walk-in tub](https://walkintubshouston.com/paying-for-a-walk-in-tub-houston/): Original Medicare generally does not pay; VA HISA grant ($6,800 or $2,000 lifetime) through the Michael E. DeBakey VA; Texas Medicaid STAR+PLUS minor home modifications ($7,500 lifetime limit plus $300 a year for repairs, per the HHS STAR+PLUS Handbook section 6600); TDHCA Amy Young Barrier Removal (up to $22,500); Area Agencies on Aging; IRS Publication 502.
- [Installation and permits](https://walkintubshouston.com/walk-in-tub-installation-houston/): Install steps; City of Houston permit basics; Texas licensing: no general-contractor or plumbing-contractor license, plumbers licensed individually by the Texas State Board of Plumbing Examiners, businesses offering plumbing must have a Responsible Master Plumber (Occupations Code 1301.351), homestead owner exemption (1301.051); electricians licensed by TDLR.
- [Walk-in tub or walk-in shower](https://walkintubshouston.com/walk-in-tub-vs-walk-in-shower-houston/)
- [Flood, hurricane and humidity planning](https://walkintubshouston.com/houston-flood-hurricane-bathroom-planning/): Harvey flooding, City of Houston Chapter 19 floodplain rule, Beryl power outages, what works without power, EPA humidity guidance.
- [Houston hard water and your walk-in tub](https://walkintubshouston.com/houston-hard-water-walk-in-tub/): City of Houston 2025 Water Quality Report hardness by system (main system average 135.5 mg/L as CaCO3, range 43.5 to 229; Kingwood 124; Willow Chase 163.5; Belleau Woods 129; District 82 107; District 73 97.4), USGS hardness scale, effects on door seals, jets and water heaters, upkeep routine.
- [Older adults in the Houston area, by the numbers](https://walkintubshouston.com/houston-older-adults-by-the-numbers/): U.S. Census Bureau ACS 2019 to 2023 5-year figures (tables B01001, B18101) for the 10-county Houston metro, each county and major suburbs: residents 65+, share 65+, residents 85+, and share of 65+ residents with a disability. Includes a chart with a data table.
- [Measure your bathroom](https://walkintubshouston.com/measure-for-a-walk-in-tub/)
- [Walk-in tub features explained](https://walkintubshouston.com/walk-in-tub-features/)
- [Caregiver guide](https://walkintubshouston.com/caregiver-guide-houston/)
- [Houston senior resources](https://walkintubshouston.com/houston-senior-resources/)
- [Senior bathroom safety checklist](https://walkintubshouston.com/senior-bathroom-safety-checklist/)
- [FAQ](https://walkintubshouston.com/walk-in-tub-faq/)
- [Service areas](https://walkintubshouston.com/service-areas/)
- City pages, each with local permits, flood notes, aging agency and Census figures: [Katy](https://walkintubshouston.com/walk-in-tub-katy-tx/), [Sugar Land](https://walkintubshouston.com/walk-in-tub-sugar-land-tx/), [The Woodlands](https://walkintubshouston.com/walk-in-tub-the-woodlands-tx/), [Pearland](https://walkintubshouston.com/walk-in-tub-pearland-tx/), [League City](https://walkintubshouston.com/walk-in-tub-league-city-tx/), [Cypress](https://walkintubshouston.com/walk-in-tub-cypress-tx/), [Spring](https://walkintubshouston.com/walk-in-tub-spring-tx/), [Kingwood](https://walkintubshouston.com/walk-in-tub-kingwood-tx/), [Pasadena](https://walkintubshouston.com/walk-in-tub-pasadena-tx/), [Conroe](https://walkintubshouston.com/walk-in-tub-conroe-tx/)

## Key facts

- Phone: 1-888-779-2284 (BATH). Email: sales@agingsafelybaths.com.
- Service area: Houston, Harris County and surrounding communities (Katy, Sugar Land, Missouri City, Richmond, Rosenberg, Pearland, Friendswood, Pasadena, Deer Park, La Porte, Baytown, League City, Webster, Seabrook, Galveston, The Woodlands, Spring, Humble, Kingwood, Cypress, Tomball, Conroe). For other Texas regions and statewide programs, see https://walkintubstexas.com/.
- Installer: Aging Safely Baths (https://www.agingsafelybaths.com/locations/houston-tx-walk-in-tubs-roll-in-showers/), helping families since 2012; an Ella's Bubbles dealer; also sells Hydro Dimensions, Bestbath (including RANE by Bestbath) and Meditub.
- Services: full white-glove installation (consultation, measuring, demo and haul-away, installation, walkthrough); supply-only orders with tech support included.
- Handicap showers: 30-year warranty on the entire shower; 1-year labor warranty with white-glove installation.
- Aging agencies: Harris County Area Agency on Aging 832-393-4301; H-GAC Area Agency on Aging 1-800-437-7396.
- Houston metro age 65+: about 875,800 residents (12.0%); Harris County about 543,500 (11.4%); 32.8% of metro residents 65+ report a disability (ACS 2019 to 2023).
